manifest.title: Agentgateway
manifest.author: OrcVole
manifest.tagline: Open source proxy for MCP and LLM traffic
manifest.description:
agentgateway is an open source proxy for AI traffic. It sits in front of your model providers
and tool servers and gives agents a single, governed entry point.

This package runs agentgateway on Cloudron with a clean, secure topology:

- The admin interface and UI run on the app's primary domain, behind Cloudron login, so only
  your Cloudron users can configure the gateway.
- The data plane (the Model Context Protocol endpoint and the OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint)
  runs on a separate subdomain that programmatic clients reach directly, protected by an API
  key that is generated for you on first install.

Use it to:

- Expose MCP tool servers (stdio, SSE, streamable HTTP, or remote) to your agents through one
  endpoint, with authentication and access policies.
- Put an OpenAI-compatible front door in front of one or more LLM providers, with key
  management, failover, and cost visibility.

agentgateway is an Apache-2.0 licensed Linux Foundation project. This package tracks its stable
releases and keeps the upstream binary unmodified.

Issues and questions about this package go to its public issue tracker.
manifest.changelog:
- Initial release. Packages agentgateway v1.3.1 on cloudron/base:5.0.0.
- Admin UI on the primary domain, behind the Cloudron proxyAuth addon.
- Data plane (MCP and the OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint) on a dedicated httpPorts subdomain,
  secured by an API key generated on first install.
- Bundles uv for uvx-based MCP servers; Node is provided by the base image.
- Ships a removable MCP "everything" demo server at `/mcp` so the gateway works immediately.

DATA_PLANE_DOMAIN.title: Data plane (MCP and LLM API)
DATA_PLANE_DOMAIN.description: Programmatic endpoint for MCP and LLM clients. This domain is not behind Cloudron login; it is secured by the agentgateway API key.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
# agentgateway is installed

## Admin UI

Open $CLOUDRON-APP-ORIGIN and sign in with your Cloudron account. The admin UI is on the primary
domain and is protected by Cloudron login, so only your Cloudron users can reach it.

## Data plane (MCP and LLM)

The programmatic endpoint is on the separate domain you assigned to the "Data plane" port during
install (the suggested name was `gw-api`). You can see or change it under this app's Location
settings. It is intentionally not behind Cloudron login, because automated agents and LLM clients
cannot complete an interactive sign-in. It is protected by an API key instead.

A demo MCP server (the reference "everything" server) is already wired up at `/mcp`, so you can
test right away.

## Your API key

A data-plane API key was generated on first start. The simplest way to see it is in the admin UI
(above): open the data-plane listener and look at its API key policy. The same value is also
written to the app's storage, so from a terminal you can run `cloudron exec` for this app and
`cat /app/data/.api_key` (it is also present in `/app/data/config.yaml`).

Clients send it as a bearer token, for example:

    curl https://<your-data-plane-domain>/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer <the-key>"

## Next steps

- Add LLM and MCP backends in the admin UI, or by editing `/app/data/config.yaml`.
- To enable the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint, set the provider key in this app's Environment,
  then add the route (see the README and the `config/examples/` files).
- Rotate or add API keys in the admin UI.

Until you configure an LLM, the admin panel shows "LLM config is not initialized". That is expected
and harmless: the gateway is healthy and MCP works. The OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint is a
data-plane route you add separately (see `config/examples/ollama.yaml`); it works on its own,
independent of that panel message.

The README covers the full topology, the exact client URLs, and the security model. Report issues at the project's public issue tracker.

manifest.changelog:
- Update agentgateway 1.4.1 -> 1.5.0
- Security: Go runtime updated to 1.26.5 to fix a CVE, JWT issuer and audience claims are now enforced, cross-namespace route delegation requires an explicit ReferenceGrant, sensitive request headers are redacted from trace and debug output, client-supplied moderation and routing headers are no longer trusted, JWKS targets are restricted, and Helm RBAC roles are scoped to the namespace
- LLM token counts now include prompt-cache tokens; set AGENTGATEWAY_LEGACY_LLM_USAGE_TOKEN_SEMANTICS=true to restore previous behaviour
- Backend and attached LLM policies now merge field by field instead of the backend policy fully replacing the attached policy; managed API key metadata now uses the agentgateway.dev/ prefix
- Legacy Istio identity TLV support has been removed; native mTLS must be used for workload identity in sandwich topologies
- Packaging: pin moved in Dockerfile ARG and the upstream FROM digest; no manifest, addon or start.sh change
# Changelog
All notable changes to this Cloudron package are recorded here. The package version is our own
semver and is independent of the upstream agentgateway version.

manifest.changelog:
- Base image cloudron/base 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 (Ubuntu 26.04). Base 6 ships no Node, so the package now
  brings its own: Node 24.19.0 with npm and npx (the runtime launches MCP servers with `npx`), at
  /usr/local/node-24.19.0 and linked onto PATH. The base had supplied Node 22.14.0, so MCP servers
  now run on Node 24.
- Upstream agentgateway 1.5.0 to 1.6.0.
- Security: JWT validation now enforces the `nbf` (not before) claim with 60 seconds of clock-skew
  leeway; the standalone UI stores newly created API keys as hashes by default (keys already in your
  config stay as they are); guardrails gain a `failureMode` and a provider guard failure on a
  streamed response or realtime connection now rejects the content instead of letting it through
  (set `failureMode: failOpen` to keep the old behaviour).
- Behaviour changes to check in your config: a provider base URL with no path now uses `/` (add
  `/v1` to such URLs); Anthropic Messages requests now prefer the OpenAI Responses format
  (`AGENTGATEWAY_MESSAGES_PREFER_COMPLETIONS=true` restores the old choice until 1.7); a built-in
  model catalogue now prices common public models, so USD budgets can begin to apply; standard LLM
  paths in the top-level `llm:` section match exactly unless `llm.pathPrefix` is set.
  `AGENTGATEWAY_LEGACY_LLM_USAGE_TOKEN_SEMANTICS` has been removed.
- Docs: corrected the slow-request guidance. Cloudron does not cut proxied requests at 60 seconds;
  the limit a user hits is their client's own timeout.

manifest.changelog:
- Upstream agentgateway 1.6.0 to 1.7.0. Model catalog with context windows and capabilities in
  `/v1/models` and CEL, service-tier-aware cost, request log analytics, guardrails over tool output, CEL
  filtering of MCP traffic, automatic agent session tracking, OIDC for browsers and API clients, and a
  raw YAML mode in every admin UI editor.
- Behaviour changes from the upstream notes: standalone now always encrypts MCP sessions (it generates a
  `config.session.key` in the config file when unset, so MCP sessions open across the upgrade are
  rejected and clients start new ones; set `config.session.key: disabled` to keep them unencrypted);
  prompt guards now inspect tool output by default (set `scope` to `SystemPrompt` and `Messages` for the
  old behaviour); dynamic backends cannot reach loopback or link-local addresses unless
  `config.backend.allowDynamicLoopback: true`; error responses no longer carry internal details such as
  addresses and CEL expressions (they are still logged); CEL header lookups return a list for repeated
  headers; `AGENTGATEWAY_MESSAGES_PREFER_COMPLETIONS` is removed; `llm.serviceTier` is normalised to
  `standard`, `flex`, `priority` or `reserved`.
- On first start the request log database gains new analytics columns, backfilled from existing rows,
  which can take a while on a large database.

manifest.changelog:
- Publish this package's own image, `ghcr.io/4glio/agentgateway-cloudron`, and release it from CI.
  `scripts/release.sh` replaces the twelve-step manual runbook: it builds, runs the linkage, secret,
  smoke, trivy and version gates, pushes, reads the digest from the registry, and writes that digest
  into `CloudronManifest.json` and `CloudronVersions.json` in the same run, so the feed can no longer
  name a version no image implements. `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs it with the workflow
  token, so no personal registry credential exists to leak or forget to revoke.
- Add `test/version_consistency.py` to both workflows: manifest version, newest feed entry, the
  `Dockerfile` build argument and the changelog block must agree, and the image must be pinned by
  digest in this repository's namespace.
- Split the GitHub workflow into two jobs so the trivy, smoke and version gates are not held hostage
  by the anonymity secret, which a checkout never carries.
- Add a known-vulnerability gate (`test/trivy-scan.sh`, wired into the PR checks): the built image
  and the build manifests are scanned for HIGH and CRITICAL findings, unfixed advisories are printed
  but not enforced, and a scan that cannot run fails rather than passing. See
  `docs/decisions/0005-vulnerability-gate.md`. The first run found `DS-0002` (no `USER` in the
  Dockerfile), which is allowlisted with its reason: Cloudron's root entrypoint is what lets
  `start.sh` chown `/app/data` and drop to `cloudron` via `gosu`.
- Bump uv 0.11.8 to 0.13.7 and yq v4.53.3 to v4.54.3. Both are verified against the digests the
  upstream projects publish, not just against the download. The base image ships its own yq at
  `/usr/bin/yq` (v4.53.6, unmanaged by dpkg); it is removed so the image carries exactly one yq, the
  pinned one, because the stale copy was shadowed on `PATH` but still published and still reported a
  fixable advisory.
- Bump Node 24.22.1 to 24.22.2 (patch), with the image digest re-pinned and the runtime path moved
  to `/usr/local/node-24.22.2`.
- CI publishes a CycloneDX software bill of materials for every build, from the same image the

DATA_PLANE_DOMAIN.title: Data plane (MCP and LLM API)
DATA_PLANE_DOMAIN.description: Programmatic endpoint for MCP and LLM clients. This domain is not behind Cloudron login; it is secured by the agentgateway API key.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
# agentgateway is installed

## Admin UI

Open $CLOUDRON-APP-ORIGIN and sign in with your Cloudron account. The admin UI is on the primary
domain and is protected by Cloudron login, so only your Cloudron users can reach it.

## Data plane (MCP and LLM)

The programmatic endpoint is on the separate domain you assigned to the "Data plane" port during
install (the suggested name was `gw-api`). You can see or change it under this app's Location
settings. It is intentionally not behind Cloudron login, because automated agents and LLM clients
cannot complete an interactive sign-in. It is protected by an API key instead.

A demo MCP server (the reference "everything" server) is already wired up at `/mcp`, so you can
test right away.

## Your API key

A data-plane API key was generated on first start. The simplest way to see it is in the admin UI
(above): open the data-plane listener and look at its API key policy. The same value is also
written to the app's storage, so from a terminal you can run `cloudron exec` for this app and
`cat /app/data/.api_key` (it is also present in `/app/data/config.yaml`).

Clients send it as a bearer token, for example:

    curl https://<your-data-plane-domain>/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer <the-key>"

## Next steps

- Add LLM and MCP backends in the admin UI, or by editing `/app/data/config.yaml`.
- To enable the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint, set the provider key in this app's Environment,
  then add the route (see the README and the `config/examples/` files).
- Rotate or add API keys in the admin UI.

Until you configure an LLM, the admin panel shows "LLM config is not initialized". That is expected
and harmless: the gateway is healthy and MCP works. The OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint is a
data-plane route you add separately (see `config/examples/ollama.yaml`); it works on its own,
independent of that panel message.

The README covers the full topology, the exact client URLs, and the security model. Report issues at the project's public issue tracker.
